Wow! What a trip down memory lane! My story with this game might differ somewhat from others, as it was a part of my childhood but I didn't actually play it. No, my cousin did. Neither of us spoke English nor were we especially bright with this type of game, as we were quite young. For that reason, we didn't go very far. I distinctively recall he restarted the game a lot for whatever reason, so quite a considerable amount of time was spent at Citadel Island specifically.

Fast forward nearly 30 years and I *finally* get to play it for myself after eyeing it here on Steam for a few years now and after refunding the first game for not being particularly impressed by it. I'm just a few minutes in, feeling like a child again running around Citadel Island not really knowing what to do (except I now speak English fluently, so I'm learning how to progress) and good God, they really don't make games like this anymore. There's something really special about LBA2 and it clicked for me immediately. It's not just nostalgia either as I didn't personally play it.

I'm also quite surprised by how well it plays on the Steam Deck. Not because I expected it to perform poorly, but because the controls are phenomenal. I made no changes to the default control scheme and despite being unorthodox even by 1997 standards, it just makes sense. In fact, I think having RT as forwards and LT as backwards makes perfect sense with tank controls. I don't recall actually playing this game much if at all (besides watching my cousin explore Citadel Island), let alone with a controller, and it feels like riding a bike... if I hadn't learned how to ride one.

I'd definitely recommend getting this whether you played it or was exposed to it as a child, or if you heard of it just recently. It actually aged surprisingly well, although parts of it do look and feel dated. It's a very unique game, the likes of which you'll struggle to find nowadays.

Après un premier épisode fort réussi, Adeline Software nous fait retourner sur Twinsun, menacée par un étrange peuple venu de l’espace. Twinsen, héros reconnu, marié et futur père, se retrouve embarqué dans un sinistre complot visant à faire accomplir une ancienne prophétie qui annoncerait la renaissance de la planète Zeelich… après la destruction de Twinsun !

Une fois encore, le joueur se promène dans le monde coloré et varié de Twinsun, qui se retrouve cette fois tout en 3D (les extérieurs, en tout cas). Twinsen doit explorer des lieux déjà connus, et de nouvelles terres lointaines. Face à vous, des créatures improbables, des peuples mystérieux.

De belles cinématiques, des graphismes améliorés, un bestiaire encore plus délirant, mais dommage seulement que les musiques soient moins prenantes (une scène de bataille générale avec une musique de promenade pépère en arrière-plan, ça n’est pas crédible). Si vous avez aimé le premier épisode, vous ne serez pas déçu par celui-ci.

I played this game first time when I was probably like 5-6, something like that, so around 2000ish. I was, and still am, living in Estonia and at that time, in close post-soviet era, there really wasnt many games around that time... even not many computers or consoles as a matter of fact. Luckily, my dad had some buddies from USA (or some other foreign country, cant really remember) and through those connections we managed to get a computer for whole family. You know, a clunky old box with a monitor built in. This game also came along with this purchase. So, I  watched my dad play the game, I watched my mum play the game (to my knowledge for her still yhe only PC game she ever played) and once I was big enough to use PC myself, me and my brother played the game, sharing computer time with whole family and all... Good memories. 

When I was young adult, say about 20 or so, I wanted to play this game again. I had the CD but my laptop couldnt play a game this old anymore.  I tried emulator, but couldnt get it to work. I tried looking up a youtube playthrough, to satisfy my need for nostalgia, but couldnt find any. I couldnt even find a forum or something, where this game was discussed. Felt quite down.

Then randomly in 2024 (2 days before writing this) I once again remembered the game and started to google it. Found out, the game had found a second life, as it was uploaded to Steam, made complicable with modern PC-s and even had a remake. Immediatedly downloaded it and finished it in 2 days. The old memories man... It was like I was a kid again... I was in heaven for 2 evenings. 

Now it might be a nostalgia speaking, and it definetly is a factor for me personally, but I must say, it is one of the best stories I have experienced in a game, especially if you take into consideration that its made in late 90s. I cant really say exactly what makes it so good, but even if its at times childish, its engaging all the way to the end. Also, the world feels alive, the NPCs for some reason dont seem to be brainless. Landscape, although small compared to todays open-world games, is interesting and in a way beautiful. It really feels like there was just regular life going on in the game. Way before its time. The controls were bad though, had to relearn how to play with arrow keys for example, but it doesnt take away from the overall experience.

Anyways, thanks to the devs and others, who resurrected LBA2 and I hope this franchise will continue to exist...perhaps a LBA3 some day, that will give this world proper justice and exposure it deserves in a modern game setting... Heres hoping

La secuela de Little Big Adventure probablemente se asentó en la memoria de los viejos usuarios de MS-DOS con mayor firmeza que su predecesor. Pues aunque LBA2 mantuviera la vista isométrica del título base en escenarios interiores, en exteriores brindaba entornos 3D, más abiertos y extensos con una vista resuelta con cámaras fijas que seguían el avance de nuestro protagonista (en esta revisión podemos elegir este modo o uno cuya cámara nos seguirá "en tiempo real").

Una aventura absolutamente entrañable para la cual ardo en curiosidad de comprobar cuando y de qué forma llegará su Remake.
